summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and a history of gastrointestinal bleeding was admitted after his left upper extremity arteriovenous graft failed due to thrombosis. He presented from dialysis with no thrill or bruit but no pain or infection signs. He was hyperkalemic on arrival and received emergent dialysis via a temporary femoral catheter. The next day, he underwent a thrombectomy with mechanical and chemical thrombolysis, which successfully restored graft patency. The procedure was briefly complicated by transient hypoxia and chest pain, attributed to a small pulmonary embolism, which resolved without intervention. He remained alert and stable, with resolution of hyperkalemia and successful dialysis through the restored graft. He was restarted on CPAP for obstructive sleep apnea and discharged to extended care with follow-up appointments in cardiology and sleep medicine. His medications, including insulin, diltiazem, and neuropathy regimen, were continued without major changes.
